title: Derived pullback along an isomorphism of schemes is an equivalence of ambient derived categories
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\Ql$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$,
uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\geq1$, and put $A=A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$
[def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be an isomorphism of
schemes on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties], and let
$D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$, $D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$ be the derived categories of
sheaves of $A$-modules on the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site].
Then the derived pullback
$Lg^*=L(g_n)^*:D(Y_{\mathrm{proet}},A)\to D(X_{\mathrm{proet}},A)$
[def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] is an equivalence of categories: it is fully
faithful and essentially surjective. (A quasi-inverse is the functor induced by the
direct image $g_*$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image] applied termwise, which is
$L(g^{-1})^*$.)

source.place: Stacks Project, Derived Categories, Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor, section Higher derived functors: an exact functor of abelian categories is computed termwise on D) applied to the exact equivalence g^{-1} of sheaf categories of lem-weil-proetale-isomorphism-inverse-image (2)-(3) and its quasi-inverse g_*; the assembly is written by an agent

proof.text: Put A = O_E / varpi_E^n. Use the exact tensor module pullback F of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] and its analogue H along the inverse scheme isomorphism. The actual coefficient comparisons are asIso of the same constant-section maps as the specified finiteTorsionDerivedPullback, so their termwise derived functors are definitionally the specified finite-level functors. The finite-coefficient realization gives the transported fixed-scalar inverse image sfIntrinsicPullback, its composition and identity comparisons. These are the published finite interface of the ordinary operations, not a new coefficient category.

Identify the right adjoint of F with the canonical constant-module direct image R of [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image]. Its coefficient map is the adjoint of the inverse-image coefficient map; homEquiv applied to homEquiv.symm rho is rho. Thus its scalar action is exactly the recorded constant-section action. Both F and the transported fixed-scalar inverse image are left adjoint to R. Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq gives their natural isomorphism. Apply this also to the inverse morphism.

Whisker these two identifications and then use sfIntrinsicPullbackComp, the equations inv g followed by g = identity and g followed by inv g = identity, and sfIntrinsicPullbackId. This gives a : F followed by H is isomorphic to the identity and b : H followed by F is isomorphic to the identity. Equivalence.mk F H a.symm b adjusts these quasi-inverse data to an adjoint equivalence e0. No assertion about sections of a fiber product is required separately.

Apply the existing source-library construction CategoryTheory.Equivalence.mapDerivedCategory to e0. It is implemented by descending the additive exact functors termwise [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization], with unit and counit obtained from the derived identity, composition and natural-isomorphism comparisons of the source library. Those comparisons are obtained by the localization universal property [lem-weil-pbc-localization-universal-property]. Equivalence.mk provides the triangle identities. The resulting forward and inverse functors are definitionally F.mapDerivedCategory and H.mapDerivedCategory. The original ambient derived categories and specified forward functor are unchanged.

The equivalence adjunction e0.toAdjunction and the canonical adjunction F to R have the same left adjoint. Adjunction.rightAdjointUniq gives q : H is isomorphic to R. Compose H.mapDerivedCategoryFactors with q applied degreewise and whiskered by DerivedCategory.Q. This is exactly the required factorization of the derived inverse through termwise canonical direct image. Its identification with the specified pullback along inv g is Iso.refl, since the inverse was constructed as H.mapDerivedCategory. These constructions work also for the empty scheme and the zero module and use neither invertibility-of-ell hypothesis.

lean.statement: theorem finiteTorsionDerivedPullback_isEquivalence_of_isIso (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (E : Type u) [Field E] [Algebra (Padic l) E] [FiniteDimensional (Padic l) E] (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n) {X Y : Scheme.{u}} (g : X ⟶ Y) [IsIso g] (_hX : ∀ x : X, IsUnit (l : X.presheaf.stalk x)) (_hY : ∀ y : Y, IsUnit (l : Y.presheaf.stalk y)) : ∃ e : proEtaleDerivedCategory Y (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E n) ≌ proEtaleDerivedCategory X (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E n), e.functor = finiteTorsionDerivedPullback l E n hn g ∧ Nonempty (DerivedCategory.Q ⋙ e.inverse ≅ (proEtaleConstantModuleDirectImage g (Padic.coefficientExtensionRing l E n)).mapHomologicalComplex (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Q) ∧ Nonempty (e.inverse ≅ finiteTorsionDerivedPullback l E n hn (inv g))
lean.note: The finite-level operation is the recorded proEtaleRingDerivedPullback specialized to the canonical constant coefficient isomorphism, with no supplied coefficient identification.
